title: Onboarding Expressway: unified ingest, transform, and gated smoke harness for community LLMs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end 'Onboarding Expressway' that accepts community LLM weight bundles, performs deterministic conversion to Redwood runtime artifacts, runs correctness and perf validation, and publishes a versioned performance profile anchored to a canonical artifact ID. The expressway must provide a gated smoke harness: lightweight functional checks, latency/throughput profiling on representative hosts, safety-signature scans, and an automatic 'anchor' (semantic version) publish only if all gates pass.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: weight ingestion API, manifest verifier, deterministic conversion jobs, artifact fingerprinting, profile synthesis (latency/throughput/kv-cache characteristics), canary run orchestration, publishing profile to catalog, generating revertable anchor.
- Out of scope: long-running continuous evaluation (will be separate monitoring job), licensing/legal review automation (manual sign-off integration).

Acceptance criteria:
- A community weight bundle (S3/HTTP/Hub URL) can be submitted and processed end-to-end with a single CLI/HTTP flow documented in the README.
- Conversion produces a runtime artifact compatible with runtime-2.4 and records a canonical artifact-id (sha256 manifest).
- Smoke harness executes on a small matrix of instance shapes and produces latency p50/p95 and tokens/s; performance profile is published when relative regressions are within configured thresholds.
- Safety and provenance checks run and generate human-readable reports; blocked artifacts create a human task.
- Every published profile is tied to a pinned artifact-id and a semantic anchor (e.g., expressway:v2026-03-10-525777).

Technical approach (high level):
1) Ingest: lightweight intake service accepts URL or upload + signed manifest. Computes provenance metadata and stores raw archive in quarantine bucket.
2) Deterministic conversion worker: containerized job that converts checkpoints to optimized runtime format (sharded CP, quantized candidates optional), emits conversion log and canonical manifest. Conversion runs in isolated k8s job with resource tags to capture GPU/runtime profile.
3) Gated smoke harness: small-size canary runs that exercise: generation latency (short prompts), streaming correctness (log-likelihood spot checks), kv-cache warmup behavior, and basic safety heuristics (toxicity fingerprint). Harness outputs machine-parseable pass/fail and human summary.
4) Profile synthesis & anchor: combine telemetry from harness with historical baselines, compute recommended serving knobs (batch size, kv cache policy, quantization suggestion) and create a profile file published to the model catalog. The artifact is anchored to canonical-id and assigned an expressway anchor tag.
5) Rollout: default publish is to staging catalog; promotion to hosted catalog requires manual approval for high-impact models. Rollback path defined: unpublish profile and mark artifact as quarantined.

Data & telemetry we will collect: conversion duration, peak memory, GPU utilization, tokens/sec under target sequence lengths, p50/p95 latency, kv-cache hit rate, mismatch counts for log-prob checks, safety-check pass rates, and conversion nondeterminism score. These map to dashboard panels and ticketable alerts in the console.

Security & compliance notes: the intake endpoint will require signed manifests or SCOPED API tokens for external submissions. All raw weights land in an encrypted, access-managed quarantine bucket. Security review required for automating any promotion that would expose artifacts to customer-facing catalogs.

Operational runbook pointers (initial): link to PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONB/Onboarding+Expressway, initial runbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-Onboarding-Runbook, conversion image repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-converters, smoke harness dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/expressway-smoke, primary alert: #ops-llm-onboard in Slack.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: Alignment with PM (Lina Ortega) and Research (Ethan Cole). Confirmed scope excludes continuous model eval; we'll hand off to monitoring after publish. Action: produce detailed manifest schema by 2026-03-05. - Aisha Kapoor

2026-03-04 - Design review: Agreed on canonical artifact-id as sha256(manifest + deterministic conversion metadata). Decided conversion must fail-safe when nondeterminism score > 0.1. Action: Marco to implement deterministic seed and reproducible op ordering. - Priya Shen
2026-03-05 - PRD link added and initial manifest schema v0.1 uploaded to Confluence. Noted edge-case: multi-file checkpoint layouts (sharded vs monolithic) require path mapping logic. - Marco Bell

2026-03-07 - First conversion PoC completed on sample-llm-1. Conversion job produced runtime bundle and manifest; small nondeterminism observed due to fused-kernel order. Opened issue: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-converters/issues/42. - Marta Ruiz

2026-03-08 - Smoke harness prototype run against sample-llm-1 on p3a.2x results: p50=78ms, p95=220ms, tokens/s=32. Safety-check flagged 2 minor phrase hits (low severity). Decision: keep as staging-only until further review. Next: add kv-cache warmup measurement and log-prob spot checks. - Ethan Cole

2026-03-09 - Security review kickoff scheduled with Security (Noah Kim). Need to confirm KMS integration for quarantine bucket and restrict convert-job IAM. Added security action item to implement least-privilege role. - Aisha Kapoor

2026-03-10 - QA testing: added unit tests for manifest schema and round-trip conversion smoke test in CI. Drafted publish gating thresholds doc: acceptable p95 regression <= +15% over baseline and perplexity delta <= +2%. Uploaded gating doc to Confluence. - Marco Bell
